fact: The World Bank status report says the Land Administration Project's Land Information System component will start new procurements to fast-track digitisation of land records and development of a digital land information system, with 0 of 200,000 land records digitised at 15 March 2024.
Minister Turad Senesi said Sierra Leone is advancing reforms to modernise land administration through digital records and is moving towards title registration.

AYV News reports on 24 March 2026 that the National Land Commission, with SLLAP support, completed a boundary harmonisation pilot using geospatial technology in Mapaki and Rogbere, as a step toward national land title registration and a land registry.

The Ministry of Lands deck (July 2025) says a Land Management Information System for cadastral and land title registration is under development at the National Land Commission with a firm recruited, and digitisation of existing land records, estimated at 60,000, is under way, both World Bank supported.

The World Bank's October 2024 status report says procurement is ongoing for digitising land records and a digital land information system in Sierra Leone, with zero land rights yet recorded under the project and the digital archive contract re-tendered.
system: Land information system (Land Administration Project P177031)

fact: The National Land Commission inspected bound paper land records at the Office of the Administrator and Registrar General on 13 February 2024 in preparation for the upcoming digitisation project of the Sierra Leone Land Administration Project (SLLAP).

The Minister of Lands said Sierra Leone is transitioning to a title registration system overseen by the National Land Commission, with digital technologies being deployed including an online portal that will let anyone verify ownership records.
system: Title registration system and online ownership portal

fact: Sierra Leone's Chief Minister said in April 2025 that the National Land Commission Act includes digitisation of the National Land Registry, with a land management information system anticipated.

Sierra Leone's land and house ownership is recorded manually, and the biometric property registration agreement with Landdreg SL ratified in December 2021 has not been implemented, per Concord Times via Sierraloaded.
system: Landdreg SL biometric property registration (not implemented)
